lines.t: If you dispense the food of God to hungry souls,
But salt it with your own, what bitterness unfolds?
Is not the flavor lost when seasoning’s misused?
The seekers come to be fed, but find their taste confused.
Oh, do not spoil the food that’s meant to heal,
With salt that taints the truth, and wounds that won’t conceal.
Serve pure and clear the manna from above,
Let every bite be filled with God’s own love.
The food of life, so rich, so vast, so true,
When mixed with worldly salt, it loses its hue.
The hunger pains within can only be eased,
When nourishment is served with faith and hearts appeased.
Oh, do not spoil the food that’s meant to heal,
With salt that taints the truth, and wounds that won’t conceal.
Serve pure and clear the manna from above,
Let every bite be filled with God’s own love.
The Word is flame, a light into the night,
A banner waving, shining ever bright.
Yet if you muddle it with bitter hands,
The hunger deepens through the wasted lands.
Oh, do not spoil the food that’s meant to heal,
With salt that taints the truth, and wounds that won’t conceal.
Serve pure and clear the manna from above,
Let every bite be filled with God’s own love.
Let every word and every seed be sown,
With salt that honors what the Lord has shown.
For those who come with hearts that seek and yearn,
Taste only Truth, and to God return.
